TotalEnergies stock: Q3 cash flow jumps as buybacks expand
sum: TotalEnergies reported stronger third-quarter performance on October 29, with adjusted net income of 9.1 billion US dollars and cash flow of 12.3 billion US dollars. The figures were published in the company's third-quarter results release.

TotalEnergies stock traded at 81.72 euros on Lang & Schwarz at 11:15 CET on Friday, November 13, 1.35 percent above the Xetra close of Thursday, November 12. The comparison uses the Xetra close of 80.63 euros from the previous session.

The energy group said gearing fell below 10 percent by the end of the quarter. Lower leverage gives the company more flexibility in balancing shareholder distributions with investment across its integrated energy businesses, although future capital returns remain exposed to oil, gas and refining-market conditions.

The board maintained the third interim dividend for fiscal 2026 at 0.90 euros per share. TotalEnergies also authorized 2.5 billion US dollars of share buybacks for the fourth quarter of 2026 and a further 2.5 billion US dollars for the first quarter of 2027. The company linked its capital-allocation policy to its objective of returning 40 percent of cash flow to shareholders.

The release attributed the quarter's performance to the group's integrated business model and geographic diversification. For investors, that mix can cushion individual commodity swings, but it does not remove the sensitivity of earnings and cash generation to market prices and refining margins.

TotalEnergies also announced a new capital increase reserved for employees, with shares offered at a 20 percent discount. The measure adds a workforce participation element to the capital-allocation agenda and could modestly affect the share count when implemented.
European energy shares remain sensitive to commodity prices, refining margins and changing expectations for shareholder distributions. See the Euro Stoxx 50 for the broader market context.

TotalEnergies or Plains All American: I Can Only Pick One Dividend Stock for the Next 20 Years. Here’s Mine
sum: - TotalEnergies yields 4.5% and Plains All American Pipeline yields 6.9% at today's prices, and both are paying more this year than last.
- TotalEnergies' dividend took 51% of its free cash flow over the twelve months to June 30, 2026, and its net debt is just 0.5x EBITDA.

- Plains All American covered its fiscal 2025 distribution 1.7x with distributable cash flow, but it carries 3.7x net debt to EBITDA and cut its distribution from $2.50 a unit in fiscal 2016 to $0.72 by fiscal 2020.
- At each stock's five-year dividend growth rate, $10,000 in Plains All American pays about $87,000 over 20 years, against about $15,000 for TotalEnergies.

If you're buying a dividend stock to hold for 20 years, the check has to make it through a few oil downturns. Both TotalEnergies (TTE) and Plains All American Pipeline (PAA:NASDAQ) are paying more this year. On Oct. 28, TotalEnergies declared a third interim dividend of €0.90 a share for fiscal 2026, 5.9% above what it paid for fiscal 2025. Plains' third-quarter distribution of $0.4175 a unit is 10% above the $0.38 it paid a year earlier.

At today's prices, Plains yields 6.9% and TotalEnergies 4.5%. (TotalEnergies sets its dividend in euros, so the dollar amount moves with the exchange rate, and France withholds tax from a US holder's dividend. Plains is an MLP, so it pays distributions on units, and holders get a K-1.)
There are over 100 stocks paying 6%+ annual dividends today.

Shell’s Nigerian Gas Exit: An Independent Investigation into the Vaaris Deals, a $600 Million Financing and the Questions Left Unanswered
sum: Shell is selling the pipeline network supplying more than 130 Nigerian businesses. Meanwhile, a separately identified Vaaris company has completed an $800 million acquisition of interests in the former Shell-operated oil joint venture. Corporate announcements, legal advisers’ disclosures and Seplat Energy’s financial statements reveal important details — and equally important limits to what can be established.

Researched and drafted with assistance from ChatGPT, using original Shell and TotalEnergies corporate announcements, Nigerian Stock Exchange regulatory disclosures, financial statements, transaction advisers’ published records, contemporaneous Nigerian reporting and historical material preserved in the Donovan–Shell Archive.

Shell is preparing to withdraw from a business that has connected Nigerian factories to natural gas for more than a quarter of a century. The proposed buyer is Vaaris Energy Limited. But the announcement comes amid another significant change in the country’s petroleum industry: a separately identified company, Vaaris Resources JVCo Limited, has acquired interests in the former Shell-operated Niger Delta joint venture in an $800 million transaction supported by $600 million in secured borrowing facilities. The transactions concern different assets, different sellers and distinct legal entities. New regulatory documents establish some of the ownership relationships behind the larger acquisition, while leaving important questions about Shell’s own gas-network sale unanswered.
On 13 October 2026, Shell announced that it had agreed to sell its entire interest in the Shell Nigeria Gas Group.
The business being sold was not an offshore oilfield, an LNG export plant or an international gas trading operation.
According to Shell, the business operated approximately 170 kilometres of pipelines across Ogun, Abia and Rivers states, supplying more than 130 connected industrial and commercial customers.
For those customers, the business provides an important physical link between Nigeria’s gas supply system and the factories and commercial premises that depend upon it.

[Investigation] TotalEnergies official coordinated with Trump to delay EU methane rules
sum: A TotalEnergies executive worked with US officials to delay the EU’s methane rules, raising questions over the company’s pledges to tackle leaks of the potent greenhouse gas.

DeSmog’s findings follow an investigation by EUobserver into US lobbying, as the EU now debates whether to delay the rules — originally due to come into force on 1 January 2027 — by either one or three years.

François-Régis Mouton, formerly vice-president of gas advocacy at TotalEnergies, has been seconded from the French oil giant since 2018 to the International Association of Oil and Gas Producers (IOGP), a London-based fossil-fuel industry lobby group.
Mouton and the IOGP have coordinated industry-backed open letters and met dozens of times with policymakers in Brussels in a push to delay the EU Methane Regulation (EUMR) over the past 18 months.
The IOGP argues that the new methane rules for oil and gas importers are not yet clear enough, create legal risks for the industry and could harm the bloc’s energy security.
Mouton, who is IOGP’s Europe managing director, met with US officials on at least three occasions to discuss the EUMR, according to social media posts.

Trump administration officials regularly cited key IOGP talking points following these meetings, including in a 27 April op-ed published in the Financial Times and an email sent to EU member states on 20 October.

TotalEnergies sells 50% stake in 1.2 GW European renewables portfolio to KKR
sum: TotalEnergies signs agreement with KKR to sell 50% stake in 1.2 GW largely developed onshore solar and wind asset portfolio across Europe for €1.8 billion enterprise value. Transaction covers assets in Germany, Spain, France, Poland; TotalEnergies retains 50% stake and continues operations. Expected completion in 2026.
*this image is generated using AI for illustrative purposes only.

TotalEnergies has signed an agreement with KKR, a global investment firm, to sell a 50% stake in a largely developed 1.2 GW onshore solar and wind asset portfolio across Europe for an enterprise value of €1.8 billion. This partial farm-down complements the company’s simultaneous acquisition of Shell’s 4 GW European renewables business, reinforcing TotalEnergies’ strategy to optimize capital allocation while expanding its power generation footprint. The transaction allows TotalEnergies to recycle capital from mature assets into new growth opportunities, supporting its Integrated Power strategy aimed at achieving a return on adjusted capital employed (ROACE) of 12% by 2030.

The sold portfolio comprises assets located in Germany, Spain, France, and Poland. TotalEnergies will retain its remaining 50% stake and continue to operate these assets after the deal closes, which is expected in 2026 subject to customary conditions. The electricity produced by these assets is either already sold to third parties or will be marketed by TotalEnergies. This structure ensures continuity of operations and revenue streams while providing liquidity through the partnership with KKR.

Vincent Policard, Co-Head of European Infrastructure at KKR, stated that the investment reflects conviction in the long-term fundamentals supporting Europe’s renewable energy sector and the critical role infrastructure plays in the energy transition. He noted that KKR is pleased to complete this new transaction with TotalEnergies and further expand its investments in Europe. This deal adds to KKR’s growing presence in the European renewable infrastructure market, leveraging its patient capital approach to support sustainable growth.

TotalEnergies Shares Methane Detection Expertise With Three National Oil Firms
sum: - SEA METEC support: TotalEnergies will share more than ten years of expertise from its TADI center to help develop SEA METEC.
- Sonangol agreement: A new memorandum of understanding expands methane and decarbonization cooperation in Angola.
- World Bank funding: The Angola partners will explore financing, including potential support from the World Bank’s GFMR Fund.

TotalEnergies has deepened methane partnerships with Petronas in Malaysia, Sonangol in Angola and Oil India (OIL). The European energy major will support the development of SEA METEC using expertise from its TotalEnergies Anomalies Detection Initiative (TADI) center. The partnerships aim to expand advanced methane detection and speed up emissions cuts.

TotalEnergies has built that expertise over more than ten years at TADI. According to the company, TADI is Europe’s only facility dedicated to evaluating methane detection and quantification technologies. SEA METEC is expected to strengthen knowledge sharing and help harmonize methane measurement and quantification methods. As a result, companies should be better able to detect, measure and ultimately curtail their emissions.

TotalEnergies linked the agreements to its commitment to the Oil & Gas Decarbonization Charter (OGDC). It did not disclose financial terms, timelines or details of its cooperation with OIL. “Our cooperation with Petronas in Malaysia, Sonangol in Angola and OIL in India illustrates TotalEnergies’ commitment to the OGDC and the momentum it has created among international and national companies,” said Patrick Pouyanné, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of TotalEnergies. “I am convinced that by sharing technologies, expertise and best practices, we can accelerate concrete action and contribute to our common ambition of achieving near-zero upstream methane emissions by 2030,” Pouyanné added.

TotalEnergies has also signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with Sonangol to strengthen technical cooperation in Angola. The agreement builds on experience gained through TotalEnergies’ AUSEA methane technology. It covers methane detection, measurement, monitoring and reduction, plus the sharing of best practices, methodologies and technical expertise.

TotalEnergies (Paris:TTE) (LSE:TTE) (NYSE:TTE) announces the signing of agreements with PETRONAS Carigali Sdn Bhd (PCSB), PTTEP and KUFPEC to acquire a 30% operated interest in the Lang Lebah and B14 gas fields, located off the coast of Sarawak, Malaysia.

Lang Lebah, one of Malaysia’s largest offshore gas discoveries, and the nearby B14 field are planned to be developed as an integrated project. This combined development is expected to unlock more than 6.5 trillion cubic feet of gas resources (equivalent to more than 1 billion barrels of oil equivalent) to supply the existing Malaysia LNG liquefaction plant with a production plateau of around 10 billion cubic meters per annum (BCMA).

“The development of Lang Lebah and B14 resources will allow the creation of another large-scale gas hub in Malaysia, leveraging shared infrastructure, to supply gas to Malaysia LNG and meet the growing LNG demand in Asia,” said Patrick Pouyanné, Chairman and CEO of TotalEnergies. “These agreements mark another important step in our strategy to strengthen our integrated gas position in Malaysia, following the acquisition of SapuraOMV in 2024 and the expansion of our long-standing partnership with PETRONAS in 2025.”
Upon completion of the transactions, which are subject to regulatory approvals, TotalEnergies will hold a 30% operated interest in both fields, alongside PTTEP (25%), KUFPEC (25%) and PCSB (20%).

Namibian oil tycoon Knowledge Katti's Sintana Energy stake falls by $3.2 million
sum: The value of Namibian oil tycoon Knowledge Katti's stake in Sintana Energy Inc. has fallen by about C$4.5 million ($3.2 million) over the past year, as the Toronto-listed explorer's shares slid despite progress on its biggest asset, a stake in one of the largest oil discoveries off Namibia.

Katti, a Sintana director, owns 23.09 million shares in the company, or about 4.13%, according to the latest disclosure of his holdings. At Sintana's current price of 36 Canadian cents, the stake is worth about C$8.3 million ($5.9 million).

When Billionaires.Africa last valued his holding in August 2025, Katti owned 22.49 million shares and the stock traded at 57 Canadian cents, which put the stake at about C$12.8 million ($9.2 million). The shares have since fallen 37%. He owns about 600,000 more shares than he did then, but the extra holding has done little to offset the drop in price.

His percentage of the company has also shrunk, from 6.02% to 4.13%, because Sintana has issued a large number of new shares. Its share count has risen by about half in a year, to roughly 559 million, largely because of an all-share takeover. At the current price, Sintana has a market value of about C$201 million ($144 million).

The share issuance came mostly from Sintana's £45 million ($60 million) all-stock purchase of Challenger Energy Group, a London-listed explorer with offshore acreage in Uruguay. The deal closed in December 2025, and Sintana began trading on London's AIM market on Dec. 23, valued at about £128 million.

Challenger brought Sintana a stake in AREA OFF-1, an offshore block in Uruguay operated by Chevron Corp., which is paying the full cost of a 3D seismic survey there. The first season of the survey was completed earlier this year, and early results are expected in the second half of 2026.

Sintana has no revenue and reported losses as it waits for its partners to drill. Its shares had already lost more than 40% of their value in 2025 by early October, before the Challenger deal was completed.

TotalEnergies has completed the transfer of its 10% interest in the Arctic LNG 2 project to NordLine, a subsidiary of Novatek. The French energy major is no longer a shareholder in the venture.

The transaction was first mentioned during the presentation of the company's second quarter 2026 results. TotalEnergies confirmed the finalization of the deal, marking a full exit from the Russian-based liquefied natural gas project.

Under the terms of the transfer agreement, TotalEnergies retains specific financial rights related to the project's funding structure. The company holds the right to be reimbursed by Arctic LNG 2 for its share of loans provided by shareholders to the project.

European Airlines and Luxury Stocks Advance as Oil Prices Slide on U.S.-Iran Breakthrough
sum: European airline and luxury goods stocks moved higher on Monday, while energy companies came under pressure after the United States and Iran announced a preliminary agreement aimed at ending hostilities and reopening the Strait of Hormuz.
The prospect of renewed access to one of the world's most important energy shipping routes triggered a sharp decline in oil prices, pushing crude benchmarks to their lowest levels in three months.

By 08:31 GMT, Brent crude had fallen 4.5% to $83.41 per barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate dropped 5.5% to $80.28 per barrel. Both contracts touched their weakest levels since 10 March, extending declines of more than 3% recorded on Friday.
The decline in oil prices weighed heavily on European energy shares.

Among the biggest movers were Equinor (TG:DNQ), TotalEnergies (EU:TTE), Eni (BIT:ENI), BP (LSE:BP.), Shell (LSE:SHEL), Neste (TG:NEF) and Repsol (TG:REP), all of which recorded losses ranging from 3.5% to 6%.
Investors reassessed the outlook for energy markets amid expectations that a reopening of the Strait of Hormuz could improve global oil supply flows and reduce geopolitical risk premiums.
While oil producers struggled, sectors that typically benefit from lower fuel costs and improving consumer sentiment outperformed.

items.t: TotalEnergies expects big Q1 earnings boost despite lower Middle East output
sum: French energy major TotalEnergies has said it expects production levels to remain unchanged in the first quarter despite having to temporarily pause operations across the Persian Gulf due to the Iran war, with the company expecting a bumper reporting period as oil prices surged.

In a trading update on Thursday, the company said that results from the exploration and production arms are "expected to rise significantly, fully reflecting the sensitivity to the increase of the average liquids price". The average liquids price has risen by $12.4 a barrel over the first three months of the year alone.

Results have also been helped by the accretive contribution from new projects, which has kept overall production in line with the fourth quarter, offsetting lost output from shutdowns across Qatar, Iraq and UAE offshore.

Operations there remain shut as a result of the US-Iran conflict, accounting for 15% of lost oil and gas output for the company. Last week, Iranian missiles had damaged its joint-owned Satorp refinery in Saudi Arabia, also causing it to shut down.

According to TotalEnergies, in a typical energy market environment where Brent crude trades between $70-80 a barrel, a $10 positive swing in the price would equate to a $2.3bn positive impact on adjusted net operating income.

Brent briefly rocketed to the $120 mark following the start of the US-Israeli bombardment of Iran at the end of February, though has come down to the $95-96 level in recent days on hopes that a peace deal between Tehran and Washington can be secured before the current ceasefire agreement ends.
LNG results and cash flow are also expected to rise significantly as a result of a 10% LNG production increase and "strong trading activities benefiting from market volatility", the firm said.

Why These 3 Oil Stocks Surged After Venezuelan President Maduro's Capture
sum: The world was stunned over the weekend by the audacious and successful U.S. raid that ousted Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro and his wife. In a Saturday press conference discussing the operation, President Donald Trump brought up how it might impact U.S. oil companies:

"We're going to have our very large U.S. oil companies, the biggest anywhere in the world, go in, spend billions of dollars, fix the badly broken infrastructure, the oil infrastructure, and start making money for the country."

When the markets reopened on Monday, however, just three oil company stocks seemed to benefit. Here's why these three oil stocks surged after Venezuelan President Maduro's capture and whether they're likely to reap long-term gains.
The market as a whole seemed unfazed by the weekend's events. The S&P 500 opened 0.49% higher than its Friday close, and went on to rise another 0.14% during the trading session.

In fact, it was only the three largest U.S. oil companies -- integrated majors Chevron (CVX +0.21%) and ExxonMobil (XOM -0.16%), and the largest independent oil exploration and production company (E&P), ConocoPhillips (COP +0.83%) -- that experienced price surges. ExxonMobil's shares were up 2.5% from Friday's close and ConocoPhillips' were up 3.1%, but Chevron was the big winner, with shares finishing up 5.5%.

No other oil stocks seemed affected. Shares of French oil major TotalEnergies (TTE -0.14%) slipped 0.35% during the session, while shares of Anglo-Dutch oil major Shell (SHEL -1.63%) sank 0.48%. British oil major BP (BP -0.02%) was up by a meager 0.87% at the end of Monday's trading. Even smaller U.S. E&Ps didn't see any benefit. Occidental Petroleum (OXY +2.04%), EOG Resources (EOG +2.08%), and Diamondback Energy (FANG -0.05%) saw their share prices drop between 4% and 5% at the start of the session, and all three stocks finished down between 0.6% and 2.9% by the end of the day.
So why did only the stocks of Chevron, ExxonMobil, and ConocoPhillips surge?
